input.task: Load the filing source and read the document identifier.

provenance: PR #56 R13. The other direction of `page_changed`, and the direction this milestone exists for: a control in the main document whose only effect is inside an iframe — an inspector's source pane, the sec-10k shape M42 leg (a) was built for. R1's repair made both sides of the comparison read `frames=False`, which fixed the false POSITIVE (every step on a framed page reading as changed) by creating a false NEGATIVE: the click really did load the document ID, `page_changed` said false, the anti-laundering guard refused a legitimate replan, and the run died `failure:act` with a reason asserting as fact that the step 'changed nothing on the page'. Both sides now read `frames=True`. That is not a third guess: it is the only setting under which BOTH directions are correct on every fixture in this repo — this case and `replan-cannot-launder-noop-action-in-a-frame` are green together, and they are the same page shape with and without a real effect. The false-positive hazard the original comment feared (a third-party iframe with a ticking clock) is now the declared ceiling: it has never been demonstrated, while this was, and this repo's rule is to widen on what a probe found rather than on what someone imagined (T-M42-14).

triage.note: the pair of cases IS the specification of `page_changed`; neither alone constrains it
